topic.title: Protein-Conditioned Molecular Design and Conformation Modeling
topic.area: Molecular, Biological, and Quantum Machine Learning
topic.overview: These papers use molecular and protein geometry to predict structures, sample conformations, and design candidate ligands. Methods combine learned representations with search, diffusion, flow matching, or physical feedback. A representative approach guides a genetic algorithm using neural models of protein–ligand structures, transferring information across targets before adapting during optimization.
topic.whyItMatters: Three-dimensional context can distinguish molecules that look plausible in isolation from those suited to a particular binding pocket. Computational scores and structural plausibility make screening more focused, although they do not establish biological efficacy or experimental binding on their own.
topic.evolution: The representatives move from protein-backbone and secondary-structure prediction toward pocket-conditioned generation and conformational ensembles. Recent work emphasizes physical feedback, faster docking, and higher-order spatial relations within pockets, reflecting several complementary routes to better structural modeling.
openQuestions: How can generated candidates be evaluated beyond docking scores?
How should uncertainty over protein conformations influence molecule generation and selection?
